text:
CData ran 378 prompts through AI agents hooked up to CRMs, ERPs, project tools and data warehouses. By its own count, competing setups got 25 to 35% of them wrong, and it traces the gap to understanding, like what a field means or whose permissions apply.

Its own Connect AI platform scored 98.5% on the same prompts. By that math it missed roughly 6 of the 378, against about 95 to 132 for the others.

The same test found the cheapest correct answers came from economy-tier models, at about 1/178th the cost of the most expensive ones, which makes a decent case for sending each request to the cheapest model that can get it right.

My read is that the accuracy gap is mostly a knowledge problem.

Here's how the new gateway learns. Every company runs on knowledge nobody wrote down, like which of several revenue fields finance treats as the real one. When an analyst corrects an agent's assumption, the fix gets proposed as shared context, a person approves it, and every request after that uses it, so a question like that gets settled once and stays settled.

It's basically how a good new hire learns a company, one correction at a time, and every request still runs under the asker's own permissions, down to individual records. I'd guess that shared layer gets more useful with every fix, and the company says it stays independent of whichever model sits on top.

Any one model is getting easier to replace. The context a company builds up is the part that carries over.

text:
the reason AI still gets so much wrong about your own company is pretty simple: most of what it needs to know was never written down

> your fiscal year starts in February
> an "active customer" means someone who bought in the last 90 days
> "behind" means under 80% of plan

all of that lives in people's heads and random old Slack threads, so when you ask ChatGPT to pull a report or check your numbers, it basically just makes a confident guess

CData just launched a gateway built for this. it plugs ChatGPT/Claude straight into the systems your company runs on, like Salesforce, NetSuite, SAP (and 350+ more) and:

> reads live data straight from the source
> holds your company's official definitions, so "active customer" means what your company means by it
> learns the unwritten rules as people use it

and when one person corrects it, the correction becomes memory for the whole company. so the next person who asks just gets the right answer w/o re-explaining

it also lives outside any single model, so if you switch from ChatGPT to Claude (or whatever model wins next year), everything it learned comes with you

CData has spent 15 years building this boring data plumbing that already runs inside Palantir, Salesforce and Google Cloud
